items.title: PESTLE is a checklist, not a model
items.claim: PESTLE analysis covers Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Legal and Environmental factors. What is its main analytical limitation?

options.text: It can predict the future with high accuracy
It generates an inventory of factors but does not weight them, link them or model their interactions — students often produce long unprioritised lists
It is legally required for UK firms
It only applies to large firms

items.reveal_title: A scanning tool, not a strategy
items.reveal:
PESTLE (originally PEST, expanded over time) traces to Francis Aguilar's 'Scanning the Business Environment' (1967). It's a structured way to spot environmental change but provides no mechanism to prioritise or combine factors.

Scenario planning (Royal Dutch Shell, from Pierre Wack in the 1970s) goes further: it builds plausible coherent futures and tests strategy against them. PESTLE feeds into scenario planning, not the other way around.
items.why: PESTLE is useful for ensuring you haven't missed an external factor. It's not a strategy tool on its own.

items.title: Small business survival rates are lower than commonly thought
items.claim: ONS UK Business Demography statistics consistently show what 5-year survival rate for new UK businesses?

options.text: Around 40% — roughly six in ten new UK businesses don't survive five years

items.reveal_title: Most new businesses don't make it
items.reveal:
ONS Business Demography data: of UK enterprises born in 2017, 39.6% survived to 2022. Year-1 survival is around 90%; the attrition is concentrated in years 2-5. SME failure causes (UK Federation of Small Businesses surveys) cluster around cash flow, late payment, and lack of management capacity.

Entrepreneurship narratives in business teaching focus on success stories. The base rate is more sobering and is one reason support programmes (start-up loans, mentoring) emphasise survival skills over growth.
items.why: Survivor bias in business case studies hides the failure rate. A textbook with only successful firms gives a misleading picture of what running a business actually involves.

items.title: The 7Ps were extended for services, not because the 4Ps were wrong
items.claim: The original 4Ps (product, price, place, promotion) were proposed by E. Jerome McCarthy in 1960. Why were three more Ps added later?

options.text: Booms and Bitner (1981) added people, process and physical evidence to capture the special characteristics of service industries (intangibility, inseparability, variability, perishability)
Because digital marketing required four extra Ps

items.reveal:
Bernard Booms and Mary Bitner's 1981 chapter 'Marketing Strategies and Organization Structures for Service Firms' added People (staff interactions with customers), Process (service delivery procedures) and Physical evidence (the tangible elements customers see).

A haircut, a flight or a consultation can't be inventoried, tested or returned. The 4Ps work better for tangible goods than for services, which by 2020 made up around 80% of UK GDP.
items.why: Frameworks evolve as the economy does. The 7Ps reflect a shift toward services that has continued since 1981.
